statements.statement: Strong consistency ensures that once a write completes, all subsequent reads will see the new value immediately.
statements.explanation: Strong consistency guarantees that after a write operation, any following read operations will reflect the most recent write. This is the hallmark of strong consistency, providing immediate visibility of the latest changes.

statements.statement: Eventual consistency guarantees that all read operations will immediately reflect the latest write.
statements.explanation: Eventual consistency allows for temporary discrepancies between writes and reads. After a write, subsequent reads might return older values until the system converges to the latest state over time.

statements.statement: In distributed systems, opting for strong consistency often results in increased latency or reduced availability during failures.
statements.explanation: Strong consistency can require more coordination between distributed nodes, which may increase latency or reduce availability, especially if network partitions or failures occur. This trade-off is often compared in the context of the CAP theorem.

statements.statement: In eventual consistency models, all nodes in the system will immediately reflect changes made by a write operation.
statements.explanation: In eventual consistency models, there is no guarantee of immediate consistency across nodes after a write. Nodes may take time to converge on the latest data, during which reads might return outdated values.
